32c92f5b0c.q: What is a blower door test and how does it measure home air tightness?
32c92f5b0c.a: A blower door test is a diagnostic tool used to measure how airtight your home is, giving an objective measured result and identifying gaps or issue areas that cause air leaks. It works by fitting a calibrated fan into an external door frame, temporarily sealing it with a flexible panel, closing all other external openings, and then depressurizing or pressurizing the building to create a controlled pressure difference while a consultant walks around searching for air leakage pathways, sometimes using a smoke pen to visualize where air is escaping.
32c92f5b0c.e: 44 Ways #35: Get a Blower Door Test
32c92f5b0c.rq: A blower door test gives you an actual measured result, identifies where leakage is occurring while there's still time to fix it and helps you ensure your home is being built to its designed and modelled energy efficiency.

f534c8d4b3.q: What air tightness level does NatHERS modeling assume for Australian homes and how often do new builds exceed it?
f534c8d4b3.a: NatHERS modeling assumes an air tightness level of 10 air changes per hour at 50 pascals for new homes achieving the seven-star energy efficiency benchmark in Australia. However, the CSIRO 2024 report on 233 newly built homes found that more than 60 percent of the results were greater than 10 air changes per hour, meaning most new Australian homes are leakier than the modeled assumption.

2cc9e3f96d.q: How much can excess air infiltration reduce the energy star rating of an Australian home compared to modeled performance?
2cc9e3f96d.a: According to the CSIRO report, in cases where air tightness is leakier than modeled, energy performance may be worse than expected, with performance potentially dropping by one or two stars or even more due to excess air infiltration alone. A six star home needs 20 to 25 percent more energy for heating and cooling than a seven star home, while a five star home needs roughly 30 to 50 percent more energy.

e498ce5196.q: What are the most common sources of uncontrolled air leakage in residential construction?
e498ce5196.a: The most common sources of uncontrolled air leakage are small gaps and penetrations at junctions between building elements and around services, including penetrations for light fittings, power outlets, exhaust fans and ductwork, wall and ceiling junctions, floor to wall junctions in suspended or slab-on-ground homes, and gaps around window and door openings. These are usually small gaps rather than dramatic failures.

a4c579fbff.q: When should blower door tests be performed during construction and why is testing twice beneficial?
a4c579fbff.a: Ideally a blower door test should be done twice: first as a diagnostic test when the building wrap, exterior cladding and roof are on and windows are in (when the building is watertight), so air leaks around penetrations or gaps can be identified and rectified fairly simply. Then another test should be done when the internal lining is in to get the final measure and check anything that might have occurred during fit-off of exhaust fans or light fittings.
